subject: Request: Standby activation grace period and RTO/RPO exception
messages:
From: Samuel Rhodes <sam.rhodes@fintrust.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@fintrust.com, Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@fintrust.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Standby activation grace period: request for temporary RTO/RPO amendment

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we move toward our scheduled compliance testing (internal audit + regulator shadow test) the FinTrust ops team has identified a narrow window where we will not be able to meet the standard 1-hour standby activation RTO for a subset of services that have cross-region KV replication. Specifically:

- Impacted services: payments-clearing and risk-scoring pipelines (namespace: ft-pay, ft-risk)
- Requested temporary RTO: 4 hours (instead of 1 hour) for the warm-standby activation window during our testing period (2028-05-01 to 2028-05-14)
- Requested temporary RPO: 30 minutes, with clear note that some near-real-time caches may not be fully persisted during the window

We understand this is an exception request and are prepared to accept additional controls (increased monitoring, joint runbook, and a temporary credit/fee uplift). We need to formalize this change in an SLA addendum and get it signed before 2028-04-15 to align with procurement timelines.

Attached is a short operations note explaining the regulatory test schedule and where the constraints come from (fintrust_operational_request_2028-03-28.pdf). Can you confirm feasibility and next steps?

Thanks,
Sam Rhodes
Head of Infrastructure Operations
FinTrust Bank

---
Attachment: fintrust_operational_request_2028-03-28.pdf (PDF, 312KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Rhodes <sam.rhodes@fintrust.com>
Cc: contracts@fintrust.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Standby activation grace period: request for temporary RTO/RPO amendment

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the heads up and the attachment. Short answer: we can support a temporary carveout, but we need to lock down the operational constraints and an addendum that outlines the conditions (scope, duration, fallbacks, and cost uplift). Before we draft language, two quick clarifying asks:

1) Exact service scope — you note payments-clearing and risk-scoring; can you confirm service IDs (or the topologies) that must be excluded from standard 1-hour activation?
2) Acceptance of mitigations — are you able to accept temporary reduced KV persistence for the testing window and the associated risk controls (increased logging, extended retention of audit traces)?

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Karthik will validate technical feasibility and provide an operational mitigation plan (KV sync cadence, warm-standby warmup steps).
- I’ll loop in Legal/Contracts to prepare a short SLA addendum draft referencing the FT-2028-042 deal id.
- Mina will propose an interim monitoring dashboard and alert thresholds we can enable for the period.

If that works, we’ll aim to circulate a redline by 2028-04-06 so procurement has time to review.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Sam Rhodes <sam.rhodes@fintrust.com>, contracts@fintrust.com
Date: 2028-04-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Standby activation grace period: request for temporary RTO/RPO amendment

Aditya / Mina —

On Sun, Apr 1, 2028 at 09:12 AM Samuel Rhodes <sam.rhodes@fintrust.com> wrote:
> Hi Aditya,
> 
> Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we move toward our scheduled compliance testing ...

I’ve reviewed the topology. Technical summary:

- Feasibility: We can provision a time-limited SLA carveout for the specified namespaces by switching affected workloads to a \"staged warm\" mode during the test window. That relaxes strict KV-replication guarantees to accelerate activation sequencing.
- Expected RTO: With staged warm mode + pre-baked checkpoints we can reliably achieve ~2 hours to activation for the impacted services. 4 hours is conservative and acceptable if FinTrust requires it.
- Expected RPO: best-effort 30 minutes; there is a residual risk of up to 1 hour for synthetic caches that are not journaled to durable storage.
- Cost/operational notes: This will require a short-term reservation of extra warm nodes and an on-call operations rota during test windows. Estimated uplift: ~18% over baseline monthly committed capacity for the period.

I’m attaching a short term worksheet and proposed addendum language (proposed_carveout_term.docx) that enumerates the mitigation checklist (runbook steps, alert thresholds, contact list). Key asks to FinTrust: explicit list of service IDs, acknowledgement of residual RPO exposure for non-journaled caches, and signoff on the on-call schedule.

If we get those items by 2028-04-05 we can draft the SL addendum and queue it for DocuSign.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

---
Attachment: proposed_carveout_term.docx (Word doc, 46KB)
Attachment: redwood_failover-diagram.png (PNG, 124KB)

From: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@fintrust.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Rhodes <sam.rhodes@fintrust.com>, contracts@fintrust.com, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Standby activation grace period: request for temporary RTO/RPO amendment

Thank you — this all looks reasonable. FinTrust accepts the conditional carveout under the following terms:

- Scope: payments-clearing (ft-pay-*) and risk-scoring (ft-risk-*) namespaces only
- Duration: 2028-05-01 to 2028-05-14 inclusive
- RTO during window: up to 4 hours accepted (FinTrust prefers 2 hours target but will accept 4 hours as the contractual maximum)
- RPO: 30 minutes best-effort; FinTrust acknowledges residual exposure for non-journaled caches
- Compensation: FinTrust agrees to the 18% uplift during the window and will process addendum approval via procurement once DocuSign is received

Please circulate a redline and the DocuSign routing link. Contracts will counter-sign as soon as the addendum is submitted.

Best,
Marta Delgado
CIO, FinTrust Bank
